practiceSet.title: U3.LT3 Practice: Model of Cell Structure
practiceSet.description: Practice the structure and job of each organelle, plant vs. animal cells, the protein pathway, cell analogies (factory, city, school), and building and fixing cell models.

activity.title: U3.LT3 Relearning: Model of Cell Structure
activity.content:
**What you need to be able to do:** I can create a model that shows understanding of basic cell structure.

**Think of a factory** (like the cell analogy project). The **nucleus** is the manager's office that holds the blueprints (DNA). **Ribosomes** are the workers who build the product (proteins). The **rough ER** is the assembly line, the **Golgi apparatus** is the shipping department, **lysosomes** are the clean-up crew, **mitochondria** are the power plant, **vacuoles** are the storage warehouse, the **cytoskeleton** is the steel frame, and the **cell membrane** is the security gate. A plant factory adds **solar panels (chloroplasts)** and a **brick outer wall (cell wall)**.

**The organelles ("little organs") and their jobs:**
- **Nucleus:** control center; contains the cell's DNA; surrounded by the **nuclear envelope**. The **nucleolus** in its center makes ribosomes.
- **Ribosomes:** assemble proteins (protein synthesis), following the codes from the nucleus. Free floating or attached to the rough ER.
- **Rough ER:** internal membrane system with ribosomes on it; makes and moves proteins.
- **Smooth ER:** no ribosomes; makes lipids (phospholipids, steroids) and detoxifies drugs and poisons (lots of it in liver cells).
- **Golgi apparatus:** proteins from the rough ER move here to be modified, sorted, and packaged, then stored or sent out of the cell (secreted).
- **Lysosomes:** the "clean-up crew"; small sacs of enzymes that break down lipids, carbohydrates, proteins, and old organelles.
- **Vacuoles:** storage of water, salts, proteins, and carbohydrates.
- **Mitochondria:** convert energy from food into usable ATP; cellular respiration happens here.
- **Chloroplasts:** photosynthesis (make sugar); found in plant cells (and algae), never in animal cells.
- **Cytoskeleton:** network of protein filaments (microtubules, microfilaments); supports the cell, keeps its shape, moves things, helps in cell division.
- **Cilia** (small hairs) and **flagella** (long whip): movement.
- **Cell membrane:** phospholipid bilayer; regulates what enters and leaves; protects and supports.
- **Cell wall:** outside the cell membrane in plants, algae, fungi, and bacteria; in plants it is made of cellulose; support and protection.
- **Cytoplasm:** gel-like material inside the membrane that holds the organelles (not an organelle; the cytosol is 70 to 90% water).

**Plant vs. animal:** plant cells have a **rigid cell wall** (plus a membrane), **chloroplasts**, and **one large central vacuole** for water and support. Animal cells have a **cell membrane only**, **no chloroplasts**, and **many small vacuoles**.

**Worked example 1:** How does a cell make a protein and send it out? Step 1: The **nucleus** holds the instructions (DNA). Step 2: A **ribosome** on the rough ER assembles the protein. Step 3: The **rough ER** moves it along. Step 4: The **Golgi** modifies, sorts, and packages it. Step 5: It leaves through the **cell membrane**.

**Worked example 2:** A student's plant cell model has a nucleus, mitochondria, and a cell membrane. What is missing? Step 1: List the plant-only features: cell wall, chloroplasts, large central vacuole. Step 2: Check the model: none of them are there. **Answer:** add a cell wall outside the membrane, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole. Right now it is an animal cell.

**Worked example 3:** White blood cells swallow and digest bacteria all day. Which organelle should they have lots of? Step 1: Digesting takes enzymes that break things down. Step 2: Lysosomes are sacs of digestive enzymes (the clean-up crew). **Answer:** lysosomes. A cell's parts match its job.

**Watch out for:** saying the cell wall controls what enters (that is the membrane); forgetting that plant cells have a membrane inside the wall; putting chloroplasts or a cell wall in an animal cell; calling the cytoplasm an organelle; mixing up rough ER (ribosomes, proteins) and smooth ER (lipids, detox); and mixing up cilia (short hairs) and flagella (long whip).
prompts: For each organelle, write one line with its job and whether it is found in plant cells, animal cells, or both (example: Mitochondria – make ATP from food – both).
Pick a business, school, or city. Write a cell analogy that matches at least six organelles to its parts, and explain each match.
On paper, draw a plant cell and an animal cell side by side. In the box, name the three structures only the plant cell has and describe where each one sits in the cell.
Trace the path of a protein from the nucleus to the outside of the cell. Name each organelle and its job along the way.
